results: 1. pupil examination (size, light reaction): mild anisocoria; the RIGHT pupil is unreactive to dim light, with involuntary pupillary spasms that are irregular in both frequency and duration and unrelated to eye position
2. MRI orbits: atrophy of the extraocular muscles, particularly the medial rectus - a long-standing, not acute, palsy
3. CT / MR angiography (circle of Willis): NO aneurysm
4. ocular surgical history: previous strabismus surgery and levator muscle surgery
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Congenital right third nerve palsy with pupillary involvement (chronic, complete, with pupillary athetosis)

Differentials to consider:
1. Old traumatic third nerve palsy (patient may not recall childhood injury)
2. Chronic compressive lesion (cavernous sinus/superior orbital fissure) not detected on CTA but present in the past and now resolved
3. Congenital cranial dysinnervation disorder (e.g., atypical Duane's with third nerve involvement)
dx: Congenital right third nerve palsy with pupillary involvement (chronic, complete, with pupillary athetosis)
